findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda environment variables block, so they are committed to source control and visible to anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or read access to the state file.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which hold secrets here) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are returned in cleartext by the Lambda API to any principal able to describe the function.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unpatched.

The function has no vpc_config, so it runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network boundary controls, easing exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the function is compromised.
